commits.subject: feat(health): DD-leg absolute-calibration coverage + evidence-proportionate tiers
commits.body:
The 2026-07-12 DD-leg analysis (docs/audit/2026-07-12-dd-leg-calibration.md)
found a season-long DD shortfall (25/42 = 0.595 realized vs 0.734 stated,
tail p=0.035) that NO monitor could see: every DD-relevant check is
drift-framed (chronic spans both windows → drift ≈ 0) and the only
absolute-level check watched [0.75,0.80) while 38/42 DD legs sit below
0.76. Pooling can't fix it — calibrated primaries dilute the band to
+10.3pp, under the WARN bar.

- realized_calibration: bucket spec generalized to a slot-aware list —
  [0.75,0.80) both slots (unchanged) + [0.70,0.75) double_down-only (new;
  live 30d reading +36.6pp at n=8). Per-bucket incident_key (composes with
  the same-day DM dedup); legacy bucket_low/high overrides translated with
  a warning instead of dying silently (review r2#7)
- slot grading priority now slot_results (production live-feed grading,
  authoritative) → PA-frame join → day-result proxy (primary on non-DD
  days only — the knowingly-biased legacy DD fallback is excluded)
- evidence-proportionate CRITICAL: requires bucket n≥20 (SE≈10pp at the
  25pp bar) OR an exact Poisson-binomial tail ≤1e-3 (0-for-8 at 0.73 =
  2.8e-5 — pipeline-failure signatures must not hide behind the n gate,
  review r2#4; 2-for-8 at 0.0064 stays WARN)
- attention streaks keyed by incident identity (r2#3: bucket A warning
  yesterday must not label bucket B's first WARN '2nd consecutive day');
  realized_calibration joins the WARN-attention list so persistence
  actually reaches the DM digest
- predicted_vs_realized drift_warn 0.08 → 0.15: the production-clock null
  simulation (see companion commit) shows 0.08 would feed the two-
  consecutive-day digest in ~69% of calibrated seasons — overlapping
  windows make crossings serially persistent; 0.15 ≈ 13%/season. INFO 0.05
  keeps low drifts visible in logs
- dd_pair/same_team_corr docstring records the chronic-blindness property
